todays_goal: Review inference as the weakest reading skill from Day 17.

lessons.subject: literature
lessons.previous_learning: Day 17 answers often stayed at the plot level instead of explaining what details implied.
lessons.course_context: Deliberate review using clue -> what you know -> inference.
learning_objectives: Support an inference with a clue.
lessons.why_it_matters: Strong readers explain what details suggest, not only what happened.

vocabulary.definition: a conclusion supported by clues and what you already know
a specific detail supporting an inference

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: point to the clue, say what it usually means, then state what you can reasonably conclude.

worked_examples.title: Invitation
worked_examples.problem: Mina moves her bag when Jay approaches.
worked_examples.solution: She may be inviting him to sit.

independent_practice.prompt: What exact detail shows Amara changes her plan?
Why does Amara probably walk toward the buses?
Why does the final sentence matter?
Write one theme and one clue that supports it.

exit_ticket.prompt: What makes an inference different from a guess?
exit_ticket.answer: An inference is supported by evidence.

lessons.voice_prompt: Keep wording simple. If Atticus gives only plot, ask: What does that detail tell you? Require a clue before accepting an inference. Do not supply assigned answers.
